title: One record of what `sdb-reader read` prints
description: The command prints a JSON array with one such record per file. Every record has the same keys for its kind of file (SDW-19): file, verification and the lists warnings, errors and findings always; extraction where text could be read; sheet, statements, parser and sheets for a German safety data sheet and for no other file; parts where such a file holds several sheets (SDW-32). A file the parser broke on is named on stderr and has no record.

parser.description: What the parser noted while reading the sheet; the list is empty where it noted nothing. For a German safety data sheet.

statements.description: The label's H, P and EUH statements, each with the sheet's wording and the regulation's. Only for a German safety data sheet.

clp_expected.description: Only for a German safety data sheet: what the CLP Regulation expects of the file's label (SDW-48). Not required, so that a record written before stays valid.

sheet_count.description: How many safety data sheets the file holds (SDB-2). Only for a German safety data sheet.

cover_page.description: Whether a cover page stands in front of the file's sheets (SDB-138). It is no sheet and nothing is read from it. Only for a German safety data sheet.

display_term.description: The word on the cover page that names a display, as printed, such as "Mix-Display"; null where there is no cover page or it names none (SDB-138). Only for a German safety data sheet.

parts.description: Only for a file that holds several sheets: each sheet read on its own, in the file's order (SDB-118). The keys sheet, statements, parser and findings beside it are the file's: its sheets united.

sheet.description: The sheet's number in the file's order.

oldest_sheet.description: Only for a file that holds several sheets: the sheet with the oldest date that counts for age (revision date, else issue date, none after the day of the run); the first where several share it; null where no sheet carries such a date (SDW-45). The file's own dates stay the newest it names. Not required, so that a record written before stays valid.

findings.description: What is wrong with the sheet as a document: for a German safety data sheet, and one entry for a sheet in another language. Empty for every other file.

warnings.description: What the reading as a whole notes: that the file is no German sheet, or that its text could not be read. Empty for a sheet.

errors.description: Why no text could be read from the file. Empty where text was read.

path.description: The absolute path of the file read.

kind.description: What the file is; safety-data-sheet is a German safety data sheet, the only kind whose sheet is read.

prints_statement_codes.description: For a file that is no safety data sheet and no safety information: whether it prints at least three different H, P or EUH codes. Otherwise null.

stage.description: The reading stage the text comes from: the version of the stage and of the PDF library, as extraction_stage() names it. Two runs of different stages may differ because the text differs.

extractor.description: How the text was read: from the text layer, or with text recognition where the layer is missing.

tesseract.description: The version of the tesseract program that read the text. Only where text recognition read it, in whole or for single pages.

raw_text.description: The text before tidying. Only with --include-raw-text.

extraction.description: How the file's text was read. Missing for a file that could not be read.

version.description: The sheet's own version, as printed.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the text read, so that copies of one sheet under several names can be told.

countries.description: The countries the sheet is issued for; empty where it names none.

stated_voluntary.description: Whether the sheet says of itself that it is issued voluntarily or that no safety data sheet is prescribed for its product.

stated_article.description: Whether the sheet calls its product an article: beside the sentence that makes it voluntary, or by saying that as an article it is not subject to labelling.

sheet_required.description: Whether, by this sheet, its product needs a safety data sheet.

information_email.description: The address the sheet names for whoever answers for it: the competent person's, else an information office's. Null where no such label stands at an address. Not in records written before the field existed.

section_text.description: The text of each section the parser found, by its number.

sheet.description: What the sheet says. Only for a German safety data sheet.
The wording as the sheet prints it.

regulation.description: The wording of the CLP Regulation, where it has exactly one.

code_source.description: Whether the label prints the code, or prints only the sentence and the parser assigned the code (SDB-174).

part.description: One sheet of a file that holds several, read from its own text as a file holding only that sheet would be.

clp_expected.description: What the CLP Regulation expects of this sheet's label (SDW-48). Not required, so that a record written before stays valid.

warnings.description: What the parser noted while reading this sheet.

findings.description: The findings on this sheet's age, judged on its own dates as for a file that is this sheet: revised-in-future, issued-in-future, undated, predates-annex-ii, old-format (SDW-46). Not required, so that a record written before stays valid.

finding.description: A message about what is wrong with the sheet as a document. Where it concerns one statement, params names it as statement.

embedded_data.description: The eSDScom file embedded in the PDF. Only where the PDF carries one.

compared.description: Whether the embedded data were compared with the sheet as read: the embedded file could be read, and the PDF is a German safety data sheet.

differences.description: Where the embedded data and the sheet as read differ. Empty where nothing was compared.

unreadable.description: Why the embedded file could not be read. Only then.

version.description: The eSDScom version the file states. Only for a file that could be read.

system.description: The authoring system the file names. Only for a file that could be read.

message.description: Something the reader notes: a fixed code, the values it names, and a sentence in the language asked for (SDW-17). A program reads code and params; the sentence is for people.

code.description: What is noted. The same in every language.

params.description: The values the code names, such as the statement a finding is about.

message.description: The sentence, from the message catalog of the language chosen.

clp_expected.description: What the CLP Regulation expects of the label, from its codes, and where the label as read differs (clp_expected, BIB-25; SDW-48). Not part of the reading: the label's own signal word and pictograms stand under sheet.hazard_statements.

signal_word.description: The signal word the H and EUH codes call for (Annex I); never from the pictograms.

pictograms.description: The pictograms the H codes call for, with the precedence of Article 26.

signal_word_missing.description: The codes call for a signal word, and the label as read has none.

signal_word_differs.description: The label as read has a signal word other than the one the codes call for.

pictograms_missing.description: Called for, and not in the label as read.

pictograms_not_expected.description: In the label as read, and no H code calls for them.

pictograms_left_out.description: In the label as read and called for, but Article 26 leaves them out beside another pictogram it has.

codes_from_wording.description: The codes the label does not print and the parser assigned to the sentences it prints (SDB-174); each also stands in its list. Missing in a reading stored before.

drawing_read.description: Whether the label was looked at as drawn and every red diamond in it was named (SDB-179). Missing in a reading stored before.

states_no_signal_word.description: Whether the label states that it has no signal word, as "Kein Signalwort" (SDB-176). Missing in a reading stored before.

states_no_pictograms.description: Whether the label states that it has no pictogram, as "Piktogramme: keine" (SDB-180). Missing in a reading stored before.

condition.description: Whom the label says it applies to (SDB-191): consumers for "Obige Kennzeichnung gilt bei Abgabe an privaten Endverbraucher". Missing in a reading stored before.

condition_text.description: The sentence that names the label's condition, as printed (SDB-191). Missing in a reading stored before.

statement_conditions.description: Single statements printed with a condition, by code, such as P101 "Nur für private Endverbraucher" or EUH210 for others than the general public (SDB-192); the codes stand in the lists as well. Missing in a reading stored before.

further_labels.description: The blocks of 2.2 beside the label, in the sheet's order (SDB-188 to SDB-190): a small package's label, or a block under another regulation. None of their elements stands in this label. Missing in a reading stored before.

kind.description: What the block is: a package of at most 125 ml (SDB-188, SDB-189), a block under Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 or under Regulation (EC) No 648/2004 (SDB-190).

heading.description: The block's heading as printed; for a sentence naming what a small package leaves out, that sentence (SDB-189).

text.description: The block's lines as printed, without the heading.

omitted_codes.description: The codes a sentence says a small package leaves out (SDB-189), one by one.

codes_from_wording.description: The codes the label does not print and the parser assigned to the sentences it prints (SDB-174); each also stands in its list. Missing in a reading stored before.

drawing_read.description: Whether the label was looked at as drawn and every red diamond in it was named (SDB-179). Missing in a reading stored before.

states_no_signal_word.description: Whether the label states that it has no signal word, as "Kein Signalwort" (SDB-176). Missing in a reading stored before.

states_no_pictograms.description: Whether the label states that it has no pictogram, as "Piktogramme: keine" (SDB-180). Missing in a reading stored before.

condition.description: Whom the label says it applies to (SDB-191): consumers for "Obige Kennzeichnung gilt bei Abgabe an privaten Endverbraucher". Missing in a reading stored before.

condition_text.description: The sentence that names the label's condition, as printed (SDB-191). Missing in a reading stored before.

statement_conditions.description: Single statements printed with a condition, by code, such as P101 "Nur für private Endverbraucher" or EUH210 for others than the general public (SDB-192); the codes stand in the lists as well. Missing in a reading stored before.

label.description: What the block labels with, read like a label (SDB-188); empty for a block under another regulation and for a sentence naming what a small package leaves out.
